wa_chair_peak_northeast_buttress.overview: Chair Peak is the iconic chair-shaped summit at the head of the Alpental valley, one of the most recognizable peaks above Snoqualmie Pass. The northeast buttress is a classic moderate alpine rock climb, while the peak is equally famous as a winter mountaineering objective.
wa_chair_peak_northeast_buttress.beta: From the basin below Chair Peak's East Face, the route climbs a curving gully system on climber's right before trending up and left along the buttress crest to the summit. The technical crux in winter conditions is a short, steep ice bulge encountered partway up; in summer the route is straightforward exposed scrambling with occasional low-5th-class moves. It is commonly done in 4 pitches with a 60m rope, though many parties simul-climb sections or break it into 5-6 shorter pitches, especially in early-season snow. Short approach and moderate climbing make it very popular and prone to queues on clear winter weekends.
